messages.author: dae01c57a3c54a3a
messages.subject: Vectorizing Mixtures
parts:
Section 10.5 (pg 117 in v2.11.0) of the manual asserts that it's not possible to vectorize a mixture model. It presents the valid, non-vectorized model:

    for (n in 1:N) {
      target += log_sum_exp(log(lambda)
        + normal_lpdf(y[n] | mu[1], sigma[1]),
        log1m(lambda)
        + normal_lpdf(y[n] | mu[2], sigma[2]));
    }

where presumably lambda is a real, so it would be erroneous to try:

    target += log_sum_exp(log(lambda)
      + normal_lpdf(y | mu[1], sigma[1]),
      log1m(lambda)
      + normal_lpdf(y | mu[2], sigma[2]));

However, what if one builds up a vector of mixture proportions, one for each observation y, as in:

    vector[N] lambda_vec ;
    lambda_vec = rep_vector(lambdaN) ;
    target += log_sum_exp(log(lambda_vec)
      + normal_lpdf(y | mu[1], sigma[1]),
      log1m(lambda_vec)
      + normal_lpdf(y | mu[2], sigma[2])) ;

Shouldn't this work? Or would the overhead of creating/filling the new vector eliminate any benefit of vectorization?

--
Mike Lawrence
Graduate Student
Department of Psychology & Neuroscience
Dalhousie University

~ Certainty is (possibly) folly ~

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: Vectorizing Mixtures
parts:
> On Aug 15, 2016, at 4:51 PM, Mike Lawrence <mike....@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> Oh, I see that log1m() only works on reals, so one would need to do:
>
> vector[N] lambda_vec ;
> lambda_vec = rep_vector(lambdaN) ;
> target += log_sum_exp(log(lambda_vec)
> + normal_lpdf(y | mu[1], sigma[1]),
> log(1-lambda_vec)
> + normal_lpdf(y | mu[2], sigma[2])) ;

No, that won't work, because normal_lpdf() returns a single value
that is the sum of the log densities of the entry. We need to
write a vectorized form of log_mix, but it's not going to save much
because there's very little in the way of shared computation to reuse.

For another efficiency tip, you wouldn't want to do

> lambda_vec = rep_vector(lambdaN) ;

and then call log(lambda_vec), because it'd compute that log N times.
Instead, you'd want to do

lambda_vec = rep_vector(log(lambda), N);

so it only gets computed once.

- Bob
